headline.summary_title: Midterm relief, then an AI repricing
headline.intro_sentence: The S&P 500 lost 2.7% in a week that opened with a post-election relief rally; the loss was a repricing of AI, not a verdict on the economy. Our tactical allocation is unchanged: neutral equities, underweight fixed income, overweight cash, gold and commodities.

three_observations.headline: The damage was concentrated
three_observations.body: Technology and energy fell hard while consumer discretionary rose 2.6% and European indices were broadly flat.

three_observations.headline: Asia split in two
three_observations.body: Topix lost 6.5% while the Nifty 50 rose 8.5% and the Hang Seng 5.1%: India traded as the anti-AI market.

three_observations.headline: The hedge worked
three_observations.body: Government and corporate bonds rose on the week as the VIX jumped 32.0%.

four_drivers.intro_sentence: A Democratic sweep, state-level scrutiny of data centres, a two-sided oil risk premium and bonds acting as the hedge did most of the work.

drivers.title: A blue wave in Washington
drivers.body: Democrats won the Senate 54-44 and the House 253-162 and flipped five governorships, including Texas and Georgia.

drivers.title: Data-centre politics hit AI
drivers.body: The relief rally reversed as investors priced state-level scrutiny of power, water and permitting for data centres.

drivers.title: Iran priced for peace
drivers.body: Brent settled at $94.6 on 4 November, then rebounded towards $100 as tanker attacks resumed; the risk premium is now two-sided.

drivers.title: Bonds as the hedge
drivers.body: Treasury yields fell across the curve as markets read the sweep as lowering the odds of fiscal expansion and safe-haven demand followed the tech sell-off.

policy_note: On the policy side: a December Fed hike is back to about 75% priced and the BoE hiked to 4%; we expect the Fed, ECB and BoJ to hike in December, with US CPI (10 Nov) and Nvidia results (25 Nov) the next tests.
